source_documents.title: Unexpected dynamics of peptoid-conjugated dyad systems: ultrafast photoinduced electron transfer in off-facial arrangement

conditions_studied: acetonitrile, degassed (steady state, TCSPC, fsTA, FLUP)

reference_evidence_units.quote: The quenching of locally excited (LE) emission via PET was confirmed by steady-state (Fig. 2b) and TCSPC (Fig. 2c) measurements for both (i,i + 2)-Ac and (i,i + 3)-Ac.
reference_evidence_units.subject: (i,i+2)-Ac, (i,i+3)-Ac vs Ctrl
reference_evidence_units.statement: Anthracene LE emission is quenched relative to the Ant-only control peptoid.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Exciplex emission (ExE), resulting from the PET process, appeared at longer wavelengths
reference_evidence_units.subject: (i,i+2)-Ac, (i,i+3)-Ac
reference_evidence_units.statement: A weak red-shifted exciplex band (above 550 nm) appears in both dyads.

reference_evidence_units.quote: kinetic model reveals a four-state evolution of PET
reference_evidence_units.subject: (i,i+2)-Ac, (i,i+3)-Ac
reference_evidence_units.statement: Global analysis of fsTA resolves four PET stages.

reference_evidence_units.quote: As shown in Fig. 5f, the extracted kinetics clearly reveal faster PET in (i,i + 2)-Ac at early times
reference_evidence_units.subject: (i,i+2)-Ac vs (i,i+3)-Ac
reference_evidence_units.statement: The anthracene anion rises faster in the off-facial dyad during the first ~10 ps.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Our ultrafast time-resolved spectroscopic studies and steady-state emission results indicate the stronger quenching in (i,i + 2)-Ac than in (i,i + 3)-Ac (Fig. 2b).
reference_evidence_units.subject: (i,i+2)-Ac vs (i,i+3)-Ac
reference_evidence_units.statement: The off-facial dyad is quenched more strongly.

reference_evidence_units.quote: ultrafast spectroscopy directly captured the opposite trend: the off-facial (i,i + 2)-Ac system undergoes faster initial
reference_evidence_units.subject: (i,i+2)-Ac vs (i,i+3)-Ac
reference_evidence_units.statement: Initial PET is faster in the off-facial dyad, opposite to the ground-state geometry expectation; the paper attributes this to conformational heterogeneity.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The optimized exciplex structure of (i,i + 2)-Hexa reveals a significant conformational rearrangement along the helix when compared to its ground state (Fig. 4a and Fig. 3b), suggesting a kinetic disadvantage for exciplex formation.
reference_evidence_units.subject: (i,i+2) model hexamer
reference_evidence_units.statement: Forming the face-to-face exciplex needs large helix rearrangement in the off-facial dyad.

reference_evidence_units.quote: In contrast, (i,i + 3)-Hexa undergoes slight structural changes to form the exciplex (Fig. 4b).
reference_evidence_units.subject: (i,i+3) model hexamer
reference_evidence_units.statement: The co-facial dyad needs little rearrangement to form the exciplex.

reference_mechanisms.label: PET_ET
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Photoinduced electron transfer from DMA to excited anthracene quenches the LE emission and forms exciplex and radical-ion species, followed directly by fsTA and upconversion; initial PET is faster and quenching stronger than in the co-facial dyad.

reference_mechanisms.label: AGGREGATE_EXCITON_EXCIMER
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Weak intramolecular through-space exciplex emission between the covalently linked donor and acceptor (guideline 3.5: intramolecular excimer/exciplex), arising from PET; TDDFT exciplex geometries.

contrast_group.varied_factor: position of the DMA donor residue relative to the anthracene residue in the same 9-mer Nspe peptoid helix (i,i+2 off-facial vs i,i+3 co-facial)
contrast_group.paper_difference: The off-facial (i,i+2) dyad shows faster initial PET and stronger LE quenching than the co-facial (i,i+3) dyad, opposite to the ground-state distance expectation.
